title: Common ZPA access rule patterns and their ordering
aliases: allow any user any application zpa
block individual users within allowed group

prose.text: These rule layouts come from the help's configuration examples, and each depends on rule order.

prose.label: Allowing.
prose.text: {{group-to-segment-group}} The default block behind them is in [[zpa.policy.evaluation-order:default-access-block]], and the blank-field form is in [[zpa.policy.conditions:blank-criteria-mean-any]].

prose.label: Blocking.
prose.text: {{block-useful-for-small-groups}} {{block-few-allow-rest}} {{block-individual-in-allowed-group}} Why the block rule must sit above is in [[zpa.policy.access-rule-order:block-before-allow]].

checks.do: For a rule that blocks a few users, check that an allow rule for everyone else sits below it.
For a rule meant to block more than a few users, check whether the default block already covers them.
To find why a rule applies to everyone, check whether its application and SAML fields are blank.

group-to-segment-group.statement: To let specific users reach specific applications, a rule combines a segment group created for those applications with a SAML attribute for the users.

quotes: Create a segment group that includes the applications you want to configure policies for.
you might have a set of applications that you only want users from a specific department to access

block-useful-for-small-groups.statement: A rule that denies users access is useful when the number of users blocked is relatively small compared to the number with access.

quotes: configuring a policy rule to deny users access would only be useful for the following circumstances:
The number of users being blocked from application segments or segment groups is relatively small compared to the number of users with access.

block-few-allow-rest.statement: To make applications available to most users but block a few, a rule blocking the specific users is followed by another rule allowing any other users.

quotes: you would create an access policy blocking the specific users, then another access policy allowing any other users.

block-individual-in-allowed-group.statement: To allow a group but block individual users within it, one rule blocks the individuals on the segment group and a second allows the group on the same segment group.

quotes: You want to allow a specific group of users access to application segments or segment groups, but also want to block individual users within that group.
